subject: Live-response pacing anomaly — immediate mitigations & post-incident checklist
messages:
From: Elena Parkel <elena@velotech.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: support@velotech.io
Date: 2027-04-11T16:02:00Z
Subject: noticeable lag in live responses from convo-api

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing intermittent slowdowns in live responses from the conversation endpoint in our production traffic starting around 2027-04-11T15:40Z. The UI shows the streaming spinner for ~2.5–6s before any token arrives. This is affecting user experience on two customer-facing features (chat assist + quick summaries).

Attached is a short snippet of one failing request and a compressed set of request logs with timestamps (initial_request_logs_20270411.zip). Key details: model pinned to rw-serve-2-medium, region us-east, average prompt length ~320 tokens.

Can Redwood triage and advise an immediate workaround? If there are recommended runtime settings we can flip on our side to reduce perceptible latency, please share. We can carve out a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Parkel
Head of AI Integrations
Velotech

[Attachment: initial_request_logs_20270411.zip (zip, ~3.8MB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Parkel <elena@velotech.io>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T16:25:00Z
Subject: Re: noticeable lag in live responses from convo-api

Thanks for the report, Elena — really sorry for the friction. We've started an internal triage. Quick actions to try immediately from your side that often reduce perceived streaming latency:

- Switch the client to a streaming-fallback pattern: set a 200–500ms chunk timeout so the UI renders partial content instead of waiting for larger chunks.
- Lower max_tokens for the first response window (try 128) to get the first tokens through faster.
- If you can, temporarily pin to rw-serve-2-small for a canary subset of traffic; it trades a bit of quality for predictability.

We (Grace + SRE) are collecting the edge-shard and routing logs. Marissa is standing up a timeline and will coordinate the post-incident communication. Monica, please add the step-by-step config snippet for Elena's team.

Karthik
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: velotech_request_snippet.txt]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Parkel <elena@velotech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: noticeable lag in live responses from convo-api

Elena — quick checklist you can apply in the next 10–20 minutes:

1) Client config: set streaming_chunk_timeout=500ms and set max_initial_tokens=128. Example: 

  // pseudo-config
  convo.stream({
    model: 'rw-serve-2-medium',
    streaming_chunk_timeout_ms: 500,
    max_initial_response_tokens: 128,
    retry_policy: { attempts: 2, backoff_ms: 150 }
  })

2) If you have traffic routing control, send 5–10% to rw-serve-2-small for 30m and watch p50/p95 for first-byte latency.
3) If improvement observed, keep small-canary and we will coordinate a controlled rollout.

We'll watch your logs and share a more detailed mitigation if needed. Please let us know when you've toggled these settings.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 11, 2027 at 16:25, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the report, Elena — really sorry for the friction. We've started an internal triage...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Parkel <elena@velotech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T02:15:00Z
Subject: Live-response pacing anomaly — triage & post-incident plan

Hi Elena & team,

Update from our side after the first pass: a spike in scheduling contention on a subset of edge shards correlated with the customer traffic profile (many concurrent long-context requests). That caused larger-than-expected batching delays for streaming frames. Grace is pulling kernel/runtime traces and we are collecting KV cache hit patterns.

Planned next steps (internal + customer-facing):

- Immediate (now): Accept Monica's client-side toggles (chunk timeout + smaller initial token cap). If you can route a small percentage to rw-serve-2-small, do that now.
- Short-term (24–72h): We will deploy a throttled kernel scheduling tweak to reduce batch coalescing for long-context requests, and increase a single-edge shard's autoscale buffer.
- Medium (1–2 weeks): Ship a runtime patch that adjusts batching thresholds by request-length distribution; this will be rolled canary-first.
- Customer admin: we'll provide a concise remediation playbook and a postmortem timeline by 2027-04-20.

We are attaching a draft mitigation patch and a timeline doc for transparency. We'll also open JIRA-INC-8421 for tracking.

Marissa Cole
Incident Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: mitigation_patch.diff]

From: Elena Parkel <elena@velotech.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Live-response pacing anomaly — triage & post-incident plan

Thanks team — applied the streaming_chunk_timeout and reduced initial token cap. Observed first-byte latency drop from ~2.8s to ~0.6s for the canary cohort within 15 minutes. That's a meaningful UX lift.

A couple asks from our side:
- ETA for the runtime patch and whether it will require a hard restart or rolling canary.
- Because this impacted production peak, our procurement team will request a service credit estimate tied to SLA exposure (cc'ing Rishi for next steps).

We'll keep the canary running and share logs if anything regresses. Appreciate the quick coordination.

Elena

Subject: Re: Live-response pacing anomaly — immediate mitigations & post-incident checklist

Elena — thanks for running the canary and confirming the improvement. Quick answers and next actions:

1) ETA for runtime patch: canary rollout planned for 2027-04-16 (non-peak window). The patch will be rolling and should not require a hard restart; we'll throttle the number of affected shards per region during the rollout.

2) Credits / SLA: Rishi (cc) will follow up with the account team to open a formal SLA review and service credit estimate. We'll include the post-incident timeline and p95 impact window in that packet.

Action owners & next steps:
- Marissa: finalize timeline & postmortem draft by 2027-04-20 and share link. (postmortem_timeline_draft.md attached)
- Grace: finish kernel/runtime traces and upload artifacts to JIRA-INC-8421 by EOD 2027-04-14.
- Monica: provide a one-page playbook snippet we can embed in your internal runbook (due 2027-04-14).
- Karthik (me): schedule a 30m follow-up call 2027-04-16 16:00 ET to review canary health and rollout windows.

We'll keep you updated hourly during the canary window next week. Appreciate the partnership and your rapid reconfiguration to validate the mitigation.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
